title: Fukushima-oki earthquake, 16 March 2022, and Renesas semiconductor production
summary: A dated record of what original sources said, and when, about the 16 March 2022 earthquake off Fukushima and three Renesas factories. It exists to prove one path end to end: evidence with its own times and identity, a replay that shows only what was available at a cutoff, and a decision that stays a proposal until an authorized event says otherwise.

time_rules.observed_at: When the thing happened or was measured.
time_rules.published_at: When the source says it published, with its precision. A notice that prints only a date has precision "date".
time_rules.available_at: The earliest instant the evidence may be used in a replay: the published instant; or, for a date-only notice, the end of that day in the source's zone (Asia/Tokyo: 15:00:00Z on the printed date); or, for a retrospective source, the time it was retrieved.
time_rules.ingested_at: When McCluster stored it. null throughout: this file has not been ingested into the canonical store.
time_rules.retrieved_at: When the bytes were read for this file.

statements.text: First report: M7.3 (preliminary), depth 60 km, off Fukushima. Maximum seismic intensity 6-upper was observed in five municipalities: Tome and Zao (Miyagi), Kunimi, Soma and Minamisoma (Fukushima). None of the five is a city with one of the three factories, and the page lists no intensity for Hitachinaka, Takasaki or Yonezawa.

not_claimed: Shaking at any factory. No source here is an instrument at a factory: JMA values are public stations in the same city, and the ShakeMap maxima are for the whole map.
Any supplier or customer relationship. The notices name no customer, and none is inferred.
Any effect on revenue, earnings, a share price, an index or GDP. The four notices state none; they give losses only as days or weeks of production.
That "full capacity" means shipped output. Every recovery statement is on a wafer-input (production start) basis.
Independent verification of recovery. Recovery is the operator's own statement.

The JMA first report's release time (the page prints a date only).
Whether event-day JMA intensities for the three cities differed from the catalogue values read in 2026.
Which public station is nearest each factory, and how well it represents the site.
The geometry of every ShakeMap version. No grid was downloaded; the preferred version was not confirmed.
The operator's plant addresses as published in March 2022 (the 2026 listing was read).
Whether the lost production was recovered, and any financial effect. Later company reports were not read.
Renesas's Japanese-language notices and any exchange filing times were not compared against the English pages used here.

proposed_decision.title: Adopt operator-confirmed staging as the rule for facility cases after an earthquake
proposed_decision.authorization_note: No authorized event exists. This is a proposal written by an agent for the owner; it is approved only when a decision recorded in ai_context.decisions by the house owner says so, and that record's id, actor and time are written here.
proposed_decision.question: When an earthquake is reported near a tracked facility, what may Halo say about the facility, and when?

options.label: Stage by operator confirmation
options.detail: Open a case on the agency bulletin. Show the regional shaking as regional. Say "status unknown" for each facility until the operator or a regulator publishes. Move a facility to halted, partial or recovered only on such a statement, keep forecasts separate from confirmed states, and record a missed forecast as missed. In this case that would have shown three unknown sites for about a day, then the first notice.

options.label: Infer exposure from shaking
options.detail: State a likely facility impact from modeled or nearby observed shaking before the operator speaks. Faster by about a day here. It would have been a claim no source supported, and in this case public stations in the three cities read 3 to 5-lower while the reported loss ranged from about 2 days to about 3 weeks of production, so the inference would not have separated the three sites.

options.label: Do not open facility cases from earthquakes
options.detail: Leave earthquakes as a map layer only. Nothing is claimed, and the owner learns of a halt only from the news.

proposed_decision.uncertainty: One event and one operator. Renesas published quickly and in detail; many operators do not. A date-only notice is treated as known at the end of its day, which can understate how early it was actually known by up to a day.
what_would_change_it: A verified facility-level instrument reading or a regulator inspection report available on the event day would justify stating shaking at the site.
A second and third case in which operator notices came late or never would argue for an explicit "no operator statement after N hours" state rather than plain unknown.
A verified early ShakeMap geometry, joined in code to verified site coordinates, would justify showing modeled intensity at the site, labelled as modeled.
